newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Banespa deal may be out next week.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Banespa deal may be out next week.

text.p: A deal allowing the federal government to take over troubled Sao Paulo state bank Banespa may be announced next week, officials said.
Sao Paulo state officials said the state has agreed to turn Banespa into a federal bank under a refinancing package for Sao Paulo's huge debt with the federal government.

"Sao Paulo's controlling stake in Banespa would be transferred to the federal government, and the state would have one year to regain control of the bank by paying half of its debt with it," said a Sao Paulo state official who asked not to be named.
He said the conditions allowing Banespa to return to state control in one year are part of a recent federal package to encourage the restructuring of state banks.

Under this package, the federal government would offer loans to refinance 50 percent of state bank debt held by governments who want to retain control of their banks, instead of privatizing or liquidating them. The states then would have to come up with the rest.
Newspapers reported that, under the plan being negotiated for Banespa, Sao Paulo would pay off 20 percent of its debt with the bank through asset sales.
The remainder would be refinanced for 30 years, they said.
Sao Paulo's debt with Banespa in October was 20 billion reais, the official said.

Expectations that a solution for Banespa would come out soon caused a surge in the bank's share prices on the Sao Paulo bourse. The company's preferred stock soared 71 percent in the last four sessions.
The shares were 30.43 percent higher at 4.50 reais this morning.

Because of Sao Paulo's massive debt with the bank, Banespa has been under Central Bank's administration since December 1994. Central Bank management would be valid for one year but it was renewed for a further 12 months last December.
Central Bank officials have been quoted by newspapers that Central Bank management would not be renewed again.
